title: Owls Can't Move Their Eyes 😳
seo_intro:
How can owls turn their heads so far? An owl can rotate its head up to about 270 degrees.
Its tube-shaped eyes are locked in place, so it turns its whole head: 14 neck vertebrae, extra-wide channels around the neck arteries and small blood reservoirs keep blood flowing to the brain mid-twist.
sources_text: Johns Hopkins University study of owl head rotation (de Kok-Mercado, Habib, Phelps, Gailloud, Rhodes, 2013), reported by NPR ("How Owls Spin Their Heads Without Tearing Arteries", 2013-01-31), ScienceDaily (2013-01-31) and Smithsonian Magazine
sources: NPR, 2013-01-31, How Owls Spin Their Heads Without Tearing Arteries — https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2013/01/31/170758750/how-owls-spin-their-heads-without-tearing-arteries
Smithsonian Magazine, Solving the Mystery of Owls' Head-Turning Abilities — https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/solving-the-mystery-of-owls-head-turning-abilities-9561557/
